web.meta.description: Weekdot is a free calendar app for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. See your whole week at a glance, with day, month, year and list views, widgets, watch complications and rich alerts. Works with iCloud, Google, Outlook and Apple Calendar, subscribe to holidays and sports, and connect your calendar to Homey.
web.hero.title: Your week at a glance.
web.hero.sub: Weekdot is a fast, beautiful calendar for iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac. Day, week, month and year views, with colours, emoji and templates — on top of the calendars you already use.
web.hero.cta: Coming soon to the App Store
web.hero.note: Works with iCloud, Google, Outlook, Exchange and every calendar in the Calendar app.
web.features.title: Everything you plan, in one view
web.f1.d: See your whole week at once. Choose 1 to 7 days, start the week on any day and pinch to zoom the hours.
web.f2.d: Zoom out to a month with event names or a year with your busy days, and tap to jump right in.
web.f3.d: Move events by dragging, change their length, copy them to another day or duplicate them in one tap.
web.f4.d: Give events their own colour and emoji, or let rules do it automatically based on the title.
web.f5.d: Save events you plan often and add them in one tap. Weekdot also suggests details from earlier events.
web.f6.d: Show, hide and group calendars into sets, create new ones, subscribe to holidays or any .ics link.
web.f7.d: Your settings, templates, sets, rules, colours and emoji are the same on every device.
web.f8.d: Widgets for your Home and Lock Screen, a watch app, and complications for your watch face: up next, countdown, today, week number and three weeks.
web.f9.d: Weekdot speaks more than 30 languages and follows the language of your device.
web.f10.d: Optionally see the forecast above your days.

web.devices.sub: One app for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch.
web.faq.title: Questions
web.q1: Does Weekdot replace my calendar accounts?
web.a1: No. Weekdot has its own calendars that sync through your iCloud, and can also show and edit every calendar from the Calendar app: iCloud, Google, Outlook or Exchange.
web.a2: Weekdot's own calendars and settings sync through your private iCloud, and events in your other accounts stay there. Weekdot has no servers that store your data.
web.a3: More than 30, including English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Arabic.
web.a4: Yes. Subscribe to the public holidays of more than 60 countries with one tap, and to school holidays and flag days, or paste any .ics link.
web.privacy.title: Privacy
web.privacy.p1: Weekdot is built to keep your data yours.
web.privacy.p2: Calendar data: Weekdot reads and writes events only in the calendar accounts on your device (the Calendar app). Your events are never sent to us.
web.privacy.p3: iCloud: Weekdot's own settings, templates, calendar sets, rules, colours and emoji are stored in your private iCloud so they sync between your devices. We cannot access them.
web.privacy.p4: Weather (optional): when you turn on weather, Weekdot asks Apple Weather (WeatherKit) for a forecast for your approximate location. Weekdot does not store it.
web.privacy.p5: No accounts, no tracking, no ads and no analytics.
web.privacy.p6: Questions? Get in touch through the support page.
web.lang.label: Language
web.f11.d: Notifications on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch with the time, place and travel time. Snooze, or get directions straight away.
web.f12.d: Addresses fill in as you type. See the place on a map and tap for directions from where you are.

web.consent.title: Cookies and privacy
web.consent.text: Weekdot only uses storage that's needed to remember this choice. With your consent we also load the Inter typeface from Google Fonts, which lets Google see your IP address. No ads, no tracking.
web.privacy.cookies.p1: This website only uses storage that is needed: it remembers your cookie choice for 12 months, in a cookie called weekdot_consent and in your browser's local storage. If you open a link with a language in it, that language is remembered until you close the browser.
web.privacy.cookies.p2: Only when you choose Accept do we load the Inter typeface from Google Fonts. Your browser then connects to Google, which can see your IP address. With Necessary only, the site uses your device's own system font. No ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies.
web.f13.d: Public holidays for more than 60 countries, school holidays, flag days, sports, zodiac and astronomy, waste collection, or any ICS or webcal link. Kept up to date automatically.
web.f14.d: Choose your sport and follow clubs and competitions: football, Formula 1, MotoGP, tennis, cycling, NFL, NBA and more. Every match and race appears in your calendar.
web.q5: Which calendars can I subscribe to?
web.a5: Public holidays for more than 60 countries, school holidays, flag days, sports such as football, Formula 1, MotoGP, tennis, cycling, NFL and NBA, zodiac and astronomy, and waste collection in the Netherlands, Belgium and Norway. You can also add any ICS or webcal link. Subscriptions update automatically.

web.a6: Yes. Weekdot is free, without ads, and you don't need to create an account.
web.q7: Which devices does Weekdot work on?
web.a7: iPhone and iPad (iOS and iPadOS 17 or later), Mac (macOS 14 or later) and Apple Watch (watchOS 10 or later). On the Mac it is a real Mac app.
web.q8: Does Weekdot work with Google Calendar and Outlook?
web.a8: Yes. Add your Google, Outlook, Exchange or Yahoo account to the Calendar app on your device, and Weekdot shows and edits those calendars too.
web.a9: Weekdot sends notifications on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch with the time, the place and the travel time from where you are. From the notification you can snooze or open directions in Apple Maps. You choose up to two alerts per event, or a custom one.
web.a10: Up Next, List, Month, Week and Today for the Home Screen, in the style of Apple's Calendar widgets, plus Lock Screen widgets on iPhone. Use the arrows in a widget to page through more events.
web.q11: What can I do on Apple Watch?
web.a11: The Weekdot watch app shows your day and week. Complications for your watch face show the next event, today's date, a countdown, the events left today, the week number and three weeks at a glance.
web.q12: How do I follow my favourite team or competition?
web.a12: Open Calendars › Subscribe to Calendar, choose your country and tap Sports. Pick a sport, then a club or competition, and subscribe with one tap: all matches appear in your week and stay up to date.
web.q13: Can I see my waste collection days?
web.a13: Yes, for many municipalities in the Netherlands, Belgium and Norway. Enter your postcode and house number and the collection days are added as a calendar that updates itself.
web.q14: Can I change events from calendars I can't edit?
web.a14: Yes. Events in read-only calendars, such as subscriptions, are replaced by an edited copy in one of your Weekdot calendars, so the original stays intact.
web.q15: Can I set the start of the week and week numbers?
web.a15: Yes. Choose the first day of the week, show week numbers, shade weekends and show 1 to 7 days in the week view, as a grid of day boxes or as a time line.
web.q16: How do I try Weekdot before the App Store release?
web.a16: Join the public beta through TestFlight with the TestFlight button at the top of this page.

web.hs.start.1.a: Yes. Weekdot is completely free, has no ads and does not ask you to create an account.
web.hs.start.2.q: Which devices and versions does Weekdot need?
web.hs.start.2.a: iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 17 or later, a Mac with macOS 14 or later, and Apple Watch with watchOS 10 or later. On the Mac, Weekdot is a real Mac app.
web.hs.start.3.q: How do I join the beta?
web.hs.start.3.a: Install TestFlight from the App Store, open the Weekdot invitation link on your iPhone, iPad or Mac and tap Accept, then Install. New builds appear in TestFlight, and you can turn on automatic updates there.
web.hs.start.4.q: Do I need to create an account?
web.hs.start.4.a: No. Weekdot works with the Apple Account already on your device. There is nothing to sign up for.
web.hs.start.5.q: How do I change the language?
web.hs.start.5.a: Weekdot follows the language of your device and speaks more than 30 languages. On iPhone and iPad you can choose a language for Weekdot only in Settings › Apps › Weekdot › Language. On the Mac, use System Settings › General › Language & Region › Applications.
web.hs.cals.1.a: Allow full calendar access in Settings › Privacy & Security › Calendars › Weekdot › Full Access. Then check in Weekdot under Settings › Calendars that Show Calendar App Calendars is on, and that the calendars are switched on in the Calendars list.
web.hs.cals.2.q: How do I add a Google or Outlook calendar?
web.hs.cals.2.a: Add the account in Settings › Apps › Calendar › Calendar Accounts (on the Mac: Calendar app › Add Account). Weekdot shows it automatically, and you can create and edit events in it.
web.hs.cals.3.q: Some of my calendars are missing
web.hs.cals.3.a: Open Calendars in Weekdot and make sure they are switched on, and that you are not looking at a calendar set that leaves them out. Also check in Settings › Apps › Calendar › Calendar Accounts that Calendars is turned on for that account.
web.hs.cals.4.q: Can I use Weekdot without the Calendar app?
web.hs.cals.4.a: Yes. Weekdot has its own calendars that sync through your private iCloud, each with its own colour. You can use them on their own, or together with the calendars from the Calendar app.
web.hs.cals.5.q: How do I show birthdays and reminders?
web.hs.cals.5.a: Turn on Show Birthdays and Show Reminders in Settings › Calendars. Birthdays come from your contacts; for reminders Weekdot asks for access to Reminders.
web.hs.cals.6.a: A set is a group of calendars, for example Work or Family. Create them under Calendars › Calendar Sets and switch between them to see only what matters right now.
web.hs.views.1.q: How do I change the week view?
web.hs.views.1.a: In Settings › Views choose the start view, the week layout (a grid of day boxes or a time line), how many days you see, the first day of the week, week numbers and shaded weekends.
web.hs.views.2.q: How do I move, copy or resize an event?
web.hs.views.2.a: Drag an event to another time or day to move it, and drag its bottom edge to change its length. Use the event's menu to copy it to another day or duplicate it. In Settings › New Events you choose the steps an event snaps to while dragging.
web.hs.views.3.q: What are templates and colour rules?
web.hs.views.3.a: Templates are events you plan often, such as Gym or Dentist, that you add in one tap. Colour & Emoji Rules give events a colour or emoji automatically based on words in the title. You find both in Settings › Events.
web.hs.views.4.q: Can I change events from calendars I can't edit?
web.hs.views.4.a: Yes. Events in read-only calendars, such as subscriptions, are replaced by an edited copy in one of your Weekdot calendars, so the original stays intact.
web.hs.views.5.q: How do I change or delete a repeating event?
web.hs.views.5.a: Open the event, make your change and choose whether it applies to this event only or to this and all future events.
web.hs.views.6.q: I hid an event. How do I get it back?
web.hs.views.6.a: Go to Settings › Calendars › Hidden Events. There you see every event you hid and can show it again.
web.hs.views.7.q: How do I show the weather?
web.hs.views.7.a: Turn on Weather in Week View in Settings › Weather. Enter your town if you don't want to share your location. Forecasts come from Apple Weather.
web.hs.subs.1.q: Which calendars can I subscribe to?
web.hs.subs.1.a: Public holidays for more than 60 countries, school holidays, flag days, sports such as football, Formula 1, MotoGP, tennis, cycling, NFL and NBA, zodiac and astronomy, and waste collection in the Netherlands, Belgium and Norway.
web.hs.subs.2.q: How do I follow my favourite team or competition?
web.hs.subs.2.a: Open Calendars › Subscribe to Calendar, choose your country and tap Sports. Pick a sport, then a club or competition, and subscribe with one tap: every match appears in your week and stays up to date.
web.hs.subs.3.q: Can I see my waste collection days?
web.hs.subs.3.a: Yes, for many municipalities in the Netherlands, Belgium and Norway. Enter your postcode and house number and the collection days are added as a calendar that updates itself.
web.hs.subs.4.q: How do I add an ICS or webcal link?
web.hs.subs.4.a: Open Calendars › Subscribe to Calendar and paste the link. Weekdot adds it as a calendar with its own colour.
web.hs.subs.5.a: Automatically, in the background and when you open Weekdot. Changed match times or new holidays appear without you having to do anything.
web.hs.alerts.1.a: Weekdot sends notifications on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch with the time, the place and the travel time. From the notification you can snooze or open directions in Apple Maps. Choose up to two alerts per event, or a custom one.
web.hs.alerts.2.a: Check that notifications for Weekdot are allowed in Settings › Notifications › Weekdot, and that a Focus is not silencing them. Set a default alert for new events in Settings › New Events.
web.hs.alerts.3.a: With Weekdot Alerts for All Calendars on, Weekdot also alerts for events from the Calendar app, and the Calendar app may alert too. Turn that setting off in Settings › Notifications, or turn off alerts in the Calendar app.
web.hs.alerts.4.q: Why is there no travel time?
web.hs.alerts.4.a: Travel time needs a place with an address and access to your location while you use Weekdot. Allow it in Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services › Weekdot.
web.hs.alerts.5.q: Which widgets are there and how do I add them?
web.hs.alerts.5.a: Up Next, List, Month, Week and Today for the Home Screen, plus Lock Screen widgets on iPhone. Touch and hold the Home Screen, tap Edit › Add Widget and choose Weekdot.
web.hs.alerts.6.q: Why doesn't the app icon show today's date?
web.hs.alerts.6.a: Only Apple's own Calendar app can change its icon by itself. Add the Weekdot Today widget to your Home Screen for a live date. On the Mac, the Dock icon shows today's date while Weekdot is open.
web.hs.alerts.7.q: My widget is not up to date
web.hs.alerts.7.a: Your device decides when widgets refresh. Opening Weekdot updates them straight away. Widgets show the same calendars as the app, so hidden calendars stay hidden there too.
web.hs.watch.1.q: What can I do on Apple Watch?
web.hs.watch.1.a: The Weekdot watch app shows your day and week and the details of each event. Complications show the next event, today's date, a countdown, the events left today, the week number and three weeks at a glance.
web.hs.watch.2.q: How do I add a Weekdot complication?
web.hs.watch.2.a: Touch and hold your watch face, tap Edit, swipe to the complications, tap a spot and choose Weekdot. You can also do this in the Watch app on your iPhone under Face Gallery.
web.hs.watch.3.q: The watch app shows no events
web.hs.watch.3.a: Make sure Weekdot is installed on your watch and has calendar access on your iPhone. Open Weekdot on your iPhone once, keep your watch nearby and give it a moment to sync.
web.hs.watch.4.a: Yes, a real Mac app with the same views, sidebar and keyboard and mouse support. Your settings, templates and colours sync with your iPhone and iPad through iCloud.
web.hs.sync.1.q: Do my colours and templates sync?
web.hs.sync.1.a: Yes, through iCloud. Make sure you are signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account on all your devices.
web.hs.sync.2.q: Syncing between my devices doesn't work
web.hs.sync.2.a: Check that iCloud is on for Weekdot in Settings › [your name] › iCloud, and use Sync Now in Weekdot under Settings › Sync. Events from Google, Outlook or Exchange sync through those accounts, not through Weekdot.
web.hs.sync.3.q: Weekdot says my iCloud storage was full
web.hs.sync.3.a: When the space Weekdot may use in iCloud runs out, Weekdot removes the oldest colours and emoji of single events so syncing works again. Your events themselves are not affected.
web.hs.sync.4.a: Weekdot's own calendars and settings sync through your private iCloud, and events in your other accounts stay there. Weekdot has no servers that store your data.
web.hs.sync.5.a: No. No accounts, no tracking, no ads and no analytics. Read the privacy policy for the details.
web.hs.homey.1.q: What can Weekdot do with Homey?
web.hs.homey.1.a: Your calendar starts Flows on your Homey: when an event begins or ends, a set number of minutes before an appointment, or at a time with today's agenda. Filter on calendar or title and use the event details as tags.
web.hs.homey.2.a: A Homey Pro with the free Weekdot app from the Homey App Store, and your Homey account. Homey Cloud is not supported.
web.hs.homey.3.q: How do I link Weekdot to my Homey?
web.hs.homey.3.a: Install the Weekdot app on your Homey. Then open Settings › Smart Home › Homey in Weekdot, sign in with your Homey account and choose your Homey. Weekdot sends your events right away.
web.hs.homey.4.q: Homey says Weekdot is not linked
web.hs.homey.4.a: Tap Update Now in Weekdot under Settings › Smart Home › Homey and check that the right Homey is selected. Under Details you see each step of the connection. Make sure the Weekdot app on your Homey is up to date.
web.hs.homey.5.q: What does Weekdot send to Homey?
web.hs.homey.5.a: Your events of the coming 8 days from the calendars you choose, sent straight to your own Homey. With Hide Details on, only the times are sent, with Busy as the title.
web.hs.homey.6.a: Tap Sign Out of Homey in Weekdot. On your Homey, open the settings of the Weekdot app and choose to unlink and delete the events.
web.hs.checks.sub: These quick checks solve most problems.
web.hs.chk1: Install the latest version of Weekdot from TestFlight.
web.hs.chk2: Allow full access to your calendars.
web.hs.chk3: Sign in to iCloud with the same Apple Account on every device.
web.hs.chk4: Check that your calendars are switched on in Weekdot.
web.hs.chk5: Close Weekdot completely and open it again.
web.hs.chk6: Restart your device if it still doesn't work.
web.hs.contact.sub: Tell us what happens and on which device. A screenshot helps a lot.
web.hs.c1.d: Take a screenshot in Weekdot and tap Share Beta Feedback, or open TestFlight and tap Send Beta Feedback.
web.hs.c2.d: Questions about Homey and Flows are best asked in the Weekdot topic, where other users can help too.
web.hs.c3.d: Read what Weekdot does and doesn't do with your data.
